utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Thank you. Good afternoon, Your Honours. This is case number IT-04-74-T, the Prosecutor versus Jadranko Prlic et al.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, registrar. Today we are Wednesday, the 16th of May, 2007. I would like to welcome all the people present in the courtroom, the representatives from the Prosecution, Defence counsel, as well as all the staff members present in the courtroom. The Trial Chamber is going to hand down two oral decisions. The first one relates to the tendering of evidence relating to Witness C -- Witness CO. As we have not settled this matter, yet, the Trial Chamber is handing down an oral decision on the tendering of evidence relating to Witness CO that came to testify on 6th and 7th of December, 2006. The Prosecution submitted a request with a view to tendering some of their evidence on the basis of its list, IC 00165. The Trial Chamber has agreed to admit Exhibit P 04484 on the grounds that it is -- it contains some relevance and probative value. The Trial Chamber would like to specify that Exhibit P 0360 [as interpreted] -- let me repeat, P O three, hundred and sixty [as interpreted] -- P 03160 and P 09285 have already been admitted on the 11th of December, 2006, and 14th of December, 2006. The Trial Chamber notes that Defence teams have not asked for the tendering of any evidence as regards Witness CO. Second decision, oral decision handed down on the 14th of May, 2006, relating to the application made by Mr. Prlic with a view to having more time to conduct the cross-examination of a particular witness. At the hearing of the 15th of May, 2007, Karnavas -- Mr. Karnavas asked for extra time which was granted by the Trial Chamber so that he could conduct the cross-examination of a witness on the grounds that this witness, according to him, and I'm quoting him, "is important to his case." After having deliberated today, the Trial Chamber would like to remind all and everyone of the following: At the hearing of the 14th of May, 2007, it granted four hours to the Prosecution so that it could conduct its examination-in-chief and five hours to Defence teams so that they could conduct their cross-examination. One hour was granted to the accused Prlic, given that the testimony relates to his responsibility. Secondly, the Trial Chamber would like to recall that pursuant to its decision of the 12th of July, 2006, it allowed for the possibility to review on an exceptional basis - let me emphasise on an exceptional basis - the assessment of the lengths of time of the cross-examinations in light of testimonies of witness to come to testify in court. In this particular case, the Trial Chamber has realised that -- or realised that Mr. Karnavas did not submit any exceptional reasons which would substantiate the granting of additional time for him to conduct his cross-examination and thus sees no reason why it should review or go back on its decision, decision relating to extension of time. Therefore, the Trial Chamber feels that the cross-examination of the witness should proceed as was planned initially. However, the Trial Chamber invites Mr. Karnavas to set forth at the end of his cross-examination -- if necessary, to set forth those exceptional reasons which he feels would substantiate additional time. Lastly, the Trial Chamber has acknowledged the fact that Mr. Karnavas intends to file a written motion seeking severance. The Trial Chamber would like to remind the parties that this issue has already been addressed when the Trial Chamber ruled on the matter during a Status Conference on the 1st of July, 2006 [as interpreted]. We are now going to proceed with the cross-examination. If after the allotted time Mr. Karnavas feels that he has not had enough time, in that case he will set forth those reasons, exceptional reasons, for which he wishes to have extra time. In that case, the Trial Chamber will rule on the matter. This, of course, will be assessed in light of the questions put and the answers provided. On line 10 of page 3, this is not the 1st of July, 2006 but 1st of July, 2005. There was a mistake there. As far as severance is concerned, I would like to remind you that the Trial Chamber has already settled the matter, but nothing prevents Defence counsel from filing a new written motion if it feels there are new elements. Now, as far as additional time is concerned and given the constant litany on a fair trial for a number of days now, the registrar on the 10th of May, 2007, at 3 minutes past 4.00, gave us time allocation and breakdown. This chart mentions that the Prosecutor has had for its examination-in-chief and for additional questions 207 hours and 90 minutes. This chart specifies that Defence teams have had all in all 234 hours, i.e., 30 hours more than the Prosecution, and according to our calculations Mr. Prlic's Defence counsel has had 47 hours and 58 minutes, just about 48 hours. Now, if you divide 48 out of 207, you realise that Defence counsel 1D has had a great amount of time. Notwithstanding these figures, I would like to indicate that procedural matters have taken up 146 hours. The registry was unable to give me the breakdown per Defence counsel or per lawyer on the basis of these 156 hours, but we have every reason to believe that some time has been taken by Prlic's Defence counsel. So to conclude and in light of the figures, Defence -- the Defence teams has had enough time as compared with the time allocated to the Prosecution, has had enough time for its cross-examination. We shall consider the questions put this afternoon and decide thereupon whether it's necessary -- necessary to grant more time. The Trial Chamber I believe has granted a degree of flexibility, and given the interest of some of the questions put by Mr. Coric's Defence counsel, we did grant extra time. Also, Mr. Praljak has had some extra time, and more time than what had been planned. We shall now ask the usher to bring the witness into the courtroom so that we can resume the cross-examination, and we shall move into private session. I would like you to kindly drop the blinds, please, and I shall give the floor to the registrar. Maybe he has a number -- a few IC numbers to give us.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours, we have a few numbers to be assigned to Witness BC, who is currently on the stand. They are documents tendered by the Defence for Mr. Praljak. The first is a video extract relating to the kidnapping, which will be assigned IC number 557. The second video extract referencing the UN convoy will be given IC number 558, and a chart listing the explosion in East Mostar will be IC 559. And we have objections from the previous witness, Mr. Finlayson, and the objections are -- arise from the cross-examination of Mr. Stojic, and that will be assigned IC number 560. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, registrar. We can move into private session [as interpreted].

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Thursday, the 17th day of May, 2007, at 2.15 p.m.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 7.18 p.m.
